text:
The unemployment rate is 10.2%, which matches October 2009 (the peak). Fed funds at 0.12% and CPI YoY at -0.23% fit that month too. The 10-year yield at 3.21% is consistent with a drop from about 3.4% in September, and gold rose 12.6% in the month, which fits October/November 2009 (gold hit about $1,100 in October and about $1,170 in November).

Unemployment was 10.0% in October 2009 as first reported, and the 10.2% figure was the October reading (published in November), so the snapshot is probably October or November 2009.

Headline CPI YoY was -0.2% in October 2009, which matches. The 10-year yield ended October 2009 at about 3.38% and November at about 3.20%, so 3.21% points to November. Gold's 1-month gain of 12.6% also fits November (from about $1,040 to $1,170). US equities rose 3.1% in November, and the VIX was around 24.85 at the end of November.

The 3-month change in the 10-year of -0.19 is consistent with end-August at about 3.40%. The November CPI YoY was 1.8%, but the published October value was -0.2%, which matches the latest reading available at the end of November.

So the snapshot is November 2009.
